ProgramName: Master of Arts in Childhood Studies
Requirements: If you are applying to the MA program your application would need to include: personal statement; official transcripts; letters of recommendation – one required, two recommended. [5]
Description: The Master of Arts in Childhood Studies equips practitioners and beginning scholars with the skills and knowledge to understand and address the challenges which confront children throughout the world. [6] The program prepares its graduates to conduct research with and about children, formulate social policy on behalf of children and their families, and work effectively with diverse populations of children. [6] Graduates pursue careers in public policy, social services, youth programming, and education. [6] Rutgers-Camden's Department of Childhood Studies is dedicated to centering the study of children and childhoods in its research and teaching missions. [6] Employing a multidisciplinary approach, it seeks to both theorize and historicize the concept of childhood while also contextualizing the study of children and childhood within contemporary cultural and global settings. [6]

ProgramName: PhD in Childhood Studies
Requirements: If you are applying to the Ph.D program your application would need to include: GRE score (Note: The Graduate Records Examination (GRE) has been waived for all prospective graduate students applying to the doctoral program in the 2026-2027 academic year); personal statement; official transcripts; three letters of recommendation; writing sample (10+ pages). Description: The world’s first doctoral program in childhood studies, this Ph.D. program prepares students for careers in research, teaching, and policy-making, in which they will generate and apply new knowledge about children and childhood. The program is grounded in the sociology of childhood, which focuses on the socially constructed nature of childhood, the idea of children as social agents, and the role of social structures in shaping children’s lives. The program is also interdisciplinary, drawing on faculty and resources from across the humanities, social sciences, and natural sciences. Students in the program take courses in a variety of disciplines, including sociology, anthropology, history, literature, and psychology. They also have the opportunity to participate in research projects and to work with faculty members on their own research.

Description: The Master of Science in Biology consists of advanced coursework directed towards molecular, cellular and systems principles that apply to microbial, plant and animal contexts. You will choose between the thesis and non-thesis options. We offer non-thesis and thesis Master of Science degrees in Biology that are tailored to the student's individual career goals. A one-year non-thesis M.S. degree entails formal coursework, with no research requirement. This one-year professional degree is designed to prepare students for specialized careers on the track they choose. The thesis M.S. degree requires significant laboratory research, and a written thesis and will take 2 years to complete. The research option helps students develop scientific research skills for improved preparation for entry into PhD programs, or for direct employment in research laboratories in academia, government, and industry.

[2] The program emphasizes cutting-edge research in areas such as materials chemistry, biochemistry, nanotechnology, and molecular modeling. [2] Students benefit from small class sizes, close faculty mentorship, and access to state-of-the-art laboratory facilities. [2] The curriculum is designed to be flexible, allowing students to tailor their studies to their specific interests and career goals, whether they are pursuing a professional role in industry or planning to continue to a Ph.D. program. [2] The Experimental Track is ideal for students interested in advancing their careers in the sciences, while the Professional Track is designed for mid-career science professionals and students seeking a flexible, part-time M.S. schedule. [3]

ProgramName: Master of Science in Computational & Integrative Biology
Requirements: A transcript showing the completion of an undergraduate degree in one of the natural sciences, mathematics, computer science, or engineering. Description: The Master of Science (M.S.) in Computational and Integrative Biology at Rutgers-Camden is a 30-credit program operating within an interdisciplinary center that connects experimental and computational methods in quantitative biology. [1] The curriculum explores integrative biology, from molecular complexities to population dynamics, and utilizes computational tools for designing and analyzing experiments. [1] Students in the master's program are expected to develop strong quantitative skills and a comprehensive knowledge of systems biology, which are essential for conducting meaningful research in the field. [4] The program provides a solid foundation in key concepts of biological chemistry, biomathematics, computer science, and integrative biology. [4] Furthermore, students will gain the ability to apply quantitative approaches to biological research, critically analyze scientific literature, and effectively communicate scientific ideas and research findings. [4] Students will acquire a productive understanding of five scientific fields (Biology, Chemistry, Computer Science, Mathematics, Physics) to a level sufficient for engaging in interdisciplinary research. [3]

[2] The curriculum explores integrative biology, from molecular details to population dynamics, and utilizes computational tools for experiment design and analysis. [2] Students are expected to gain a thorough understanding of key concepts in biological chemistry, biomathematics, computer science, and integrative biology. [3] Doctoral students must demonstrate the ability to make a significant original research contribution to the field and defend it in an oral defense. [3]

Requirements: Applicants to the Master of Social Work (MSW) program must have a bachelor's degree from an accredited institution. A cumulative GPA of 3.0 is suggested, but not a strict requirement. An introductory statistics course is a prerequisite. The application requires the submission of a personal statement, official transcripts from all post-secondary institutions attended, and letters of recommendation.
Description: With the passage of the Affordable Care Act (2010) the demand for social work expertise in health has increased. This Area of Emphasis prepares students to work to promote health and rehabilitation in a variety of settings. An Area of Emphasis in Health requires three relevant courses and an appropriate practicum. Students in either the Clinical Social Work (CSW) specialization or the Management and Policy (MAP) specialization can complete this Area of Emphasis. [6]
Accredidation: The MSW program will prepare master’s level practitioners for ethical, evidence-based and critically-informed social work practice that promotes social justice, engages diversity and difference, and strengthens individuals, families and communities in local, national and global contexts. Through engagement with the program, students gain understanding in the dimensions of knowledge, values, skills, cognitive and affective processes, and behaviors as prescribed in the 2022 Council on Social Work (CSWE) Educational Policy and Accreditation Standards (EPAS). [2]
CostPerCredit: $1,099 (for 100% Online MSW program)

ProgramName: Area of Emphasis in Mental and Behavioral Health
Concentration: Area of Emphasis in Mental and Behavioral Health
Description: An Area of Emphasis in Mental and Behavioral Health requires three relevant courses and an appropriate practicum. Students in either the Clinical Social Work (CSW) specialization or the Management and Policy (MAP) specialization can complete this Area of Emphasis. The promotion of mental and behavioral health is central to the mission of social work. This Area of Emphasis prepares students to employ evidence-based interventions with a variety of client populations to promote, restore, and maintain behavioral health.
ScholarshipType: Federal Direct Loan, Federal Work-Study, TEACH Grant

ProgramName: Area of Emphasis in Social Policy
Requirements: To complete an Area of Emphasis in Social Policy, students must be enrolled in the Management and Policy (MAP) Specialization within the Master of Social Work (MSW) program. The area of emphasis requires completing three relevant courses and an appropriate practicum. [6] The application for the MSW program requires a Graduate School Application, a Social Work MSW Supplemental Application, transcripts, a personal statement, an analytic essay, a resume or curriculum vitae, and three letters of recommendation. [3] The courses may include a combination of electives, advanced distribution requirements, and an advanced social policy course. [3] These courses also count toward general academic requirements. [3] Students may also opt to enroll in relevant graduate-level courses from another Rutgers University graduate/professional school. [3] An Area of Emphasis in Social Policy requires three relevant courses and an appropriate practicum. [3] Please note, students must be in the Management and Policy (MAP) Specialization to complete this Area of Emphasis. [3]

ProgramName: Certificate in Public and Nonprofit Management
Department: School of Public Affairs and Administration
Description: The Public and Nonprofit Management certificate is offered by the Department of Public Policy and Administration (DPPA) at Rutgers–Camden. [2] This 12-credit graduate certificate is designed for professionals seeking to build leadership capacity and strengthen their impact in government or nonprofit organizations. [4] The program equips you with a core set of management tools critical to leading in today's public and nonprofit sectors, exploring key areas such as organizational behavior, budgeting, human resources, and data-informed decision-making. [4] This certificate program will allow you to advance your career in a nonprofit or government agency and develop management skills for government or nonprofit management. [2, 6] Students can pursue the graduate certificate in pursuit of a Master of Public Administration (MPA), and credits can be earned toward the MPA degree for each class completed with a grade of B or better. [2] The program is ideal for working professionals who want to earn graduate credits toward the MPA. [4]
MinimumTOEFLScore: For TOEFL exams taken through January 21, 2026, the minimum requirements are Writing 22, Speaking 23, Reading 21, Listening 17. For exams taken from January 22, 2026 onward, the requirements are Writing 4.5, Speaking 4.5, Reading 4, and Listening 4.

ProgramName: Certificate in Data Science
Requirements: The department of Statistics offers a Certificate in Data Science. [2] Students must complete 5 courses from a menu of Data Science courses. [2] Students enrolled in the Financial Statistics and Risk Management (FSRM) M.S. Program or in the Mathematical Finance M.S. Program (MSMF) at Rutgers are automatically eligible. [2] Other graduate students interested in pursuing the certificate need to apply and be approved to do so. [2]

ProgramName: MPH in Biostatistics
Requirements: Applicants for admission must have completed an undergraduate program accredited in the United States or its equivalent. Two letters of recommendation are required for Master's degree applicants.
Description: The Rutgers School of Public Health's Master of Public Health (MPH) in Biostatistics degree provides students with a clear understanding of the roles of the core disciplines in public health with sufficient knowledge of the theory and terminology used by these disciplines to allow effective participation in interdisciplinary public health efforts. The courses give students foundational and in-depth knowledge of statistical methods applied to biomedical and public health areas. Underlying theory is also introduced enabling students to learn how statistical methods are developed and applied. Students earning their MPH in Biostatistics degree will master a common set of measurable quantitative and analytic skills, as well as be able to develop and apply statistical reasoning and methods in addressing, analyzing, and solving problems in public health; health care; and biomedical, clinical, and population-based research.
Accredidation: The Rutgers School of Public Health is accredited by the Council on Education for Public Health (CEPH).

ProgramName: MPH in Environmental Health Sciences
Requirements: Students seeking a Master of Public Health in Environmental Health Sciences degree must have the following prerequisites completed: three credits in college biology, human behavior, social or health science; three credits in college calculus; and, demonstration of computer competence. [2] A statement of goals, one-to-three pages in length, which addresses: Interest in the program, Preparedness for the program, and Goals and aspirations is also required. [2]
Description: The Rutgers School of Public Health's Master of Public Health (MPH) in Environmental Health Sciences degree provides students with in-depth training on the major environmental health problems that impact the general population as well as unique, sometimes vulnerable, communities. [5] Graduates will be able to explain toxicology and appropriate dose-related responses to environmental toxicants and describe federal and state regulatory programs relating to environmental protections. [5] Utilizing their knowledge of environmental risk assessment approaches, graduates will be able to efficiently and effectively participate in interdisciplinary public health efforts aimed at ensuring population and community well-being. [5] In addition to degree coursework, students have the opportunity to attend an 8-week summer course followed by a 200-hour unpaid field training internship offered by Rutgers NJAES Office of Continuing Professional Education in preparation for the Registered Environmental Health Specialist (REHS), which are separate from earning the graduate degree. [5] Graduates are eligible to sit for the Certified in Public Health Exam. [5]
Accredidation: CEPH Accreditation
MinimumTOEFLScore: 83 for iBT, 575 for PBT. iBT subscores: Writing 22, Speaking 23, Reading 21, Listening 17

ProgramName: MPH in Epidemiology
Requirements: Application Requirements: SOPHAS application, official transcripts from all colleges and universities attended, three letters of recommendation, and a statement of purpose are required.
Description: The MPH in Epidemiology program provides students with an epidemiological approach to public health, which includes a broad overview to epidemiology, biostatistics, and the environmental influences on health, public health planning, and health services. [1]
Accredidation: All graduates also achieve the Council of Education in Public Health's public health knowledge and foundational competencies for MPH students. [1]

ProgramName: MPH in Global Public Health
Requirements: Application requirements include a statement of goals (one-to-three pages) that addresses interest in the program, preparedness for the program, and goals and aspirations. Two letters of recommendation are necessary, with at least one from an academic reference if the applicant is currently in a degree program or has graduated within the last four years. A resume or CV is also required. Submission of GRE General Exam scores is optional. Applicants who were educated in a non-native English-speaking country must provide TOEFL or IELTS scores.
Description: The Rutgers School of Public Health's Master of Public Health (MPH) in Global Public Health degree educates students on how to assess determinants of global public health in a range of contexts based on the five major public health perspectives: systems and policies, epidemiology, biostatistics, environmental and occupational health, and health education and behavioral science. [1] Graduates will have an in-depth understanding of the economic, educational, political, sociocultural, environmental, ecological, and biological conditions that impact health outcomes for worldwide populations. [9] As community advocates versed in global public health education, research, and practice, graduates will be prepared to devise thoughtful solutions to health challenges that consider the region's social determinants of health and diverse data. [9] The degree is offered 100% online or in-person. [1] Graduates are eligible to sit for the Certified in Public Health Exam. [9]
Accredidation: The Rutgers School of Public Health is accredited by the Council on Education for Public Health (CEPH). [1]

ProgramName: MPH in Global Public Health (Online)
Requirements: A complete application includes: Completion of the online application; Official transcripts from all post-secondary institutions attended; Statement of goals, one-to-three pages in length, which addresses: Interest in the program, Preparedness for the program, and Goals and aspirations; Two letters of recommendation with at least one letter from an academic reference if you are currently enrolled in a degree program or have graduated within the last four years; Resume or CV; GRE General Exam (optional); TOEFL or IELTS score for applicants educated in a non-native English-speaking country. [1]
Description: The Rutgers School of Public Health's Master of Public Health (MPH) in Global Public Health degree educates students on how to assess determinants of global public health in a range of contexts based on the five major public health perspectives: systems and policies, epidemiology, biostatistics, environmental and occupational health, and health education and behavioral science. The degree is offered 100% online OR in-person. The 100% Online MPH in Global Public Health degree gives students an in-depth understanding of the economic, educational, political, sociocultural, environmental, ecological, and biological conditions that impact health outcomes for worldwide populations. As community advocates versed in global public health education, research, and practice, graduates will be prepared to devise thoughtful solutions to health challenges that consider the region's social determinants of health and diverse data. Graduates are eligible to sit for the Certified in Public Health Exam.

ProgramName: MPH in Health Systems and Policy
Requirements: A complete application includes: Completion of the online application; Official transcripts from all post-secondary institutions attended; Statement of goals, one-to-three pages in length, which addresses: Interest in the program; Preparedness for the program; Goals and aspirations; Two letters of recommendation with at least one letter from an academic reference if you are currently enrolled in a degree program or have graduated within the last four years; Resume or CV; GRE General Exam (optional); TOEFL or IELTS score for applicants educated in a non-native English-speaking country.
Description: The Rutgers School of Public Health's Master of Public Health (MPH) in Health Systems and Policy degree trains students to understand the operational implications of health care, including the organization and delivery of health care, health economics, and health policy in the United States. [2] Students enrolled in this degree program will also utilize economic theories, concepts, and methodologies in the assessment of current health care issues and problems, such as health systems, policies, and service issues for diverse communities. From health insurance, cost containment strategies, and physician payment, to demand for health care, health regulation, and health reform, graduates will be able to ethically navigate the constantly evolving political climate of health care policy. [2] Graduates are eligible to sit for the Certified in Public Health Exam. [2]
Accredidation: The Rutgers School of Public Health is accredited by the Council on Education for Public Health. [1]
ScholarshipType: Scholarships are available, but specific types are not listed. [22]

ProgramName: MPH in LGBTQ Health
Requirements: A complete application includes: Completion of the online application; Official transcripts from all post-secondary institutions attended; Statement of goals, one-to-three pages in length, which addresses: Interest in the program. Preparedness for the program. Goals and aspirations; Two letters of recommendation with at least one letter from an academic reference if you are currently enrolled in a degree program or have graduated within the last four years. [2]
Description: The Rutgers School of Public Health's hybrid Master of Public Health (MPH) in LGBTQ Health degree is designed to support public health professionals dedicated to improving the health of LGBTQ people and populations. [4] As the first MPH concentration in LGBTQ health to be offered by an accredited school of public health, students will be prepared to address the unique health care needs of the LGBTQ community and work toward creating new policies and practices founded upon social justice and health equity. [5] Graduates will be well educated on the health disparities among LGBTQ communities as well as the concepts of gender, sex, gender identity, and sexual orientation as it is situated across public health, culture, history, legal, medicine, and the political context. [4, 5] Students, practitioners, and researchers will be trained in research practice that supports the identification of relevant health problems and opportunities of improvement in current policy to support the holistic health of this community. [5]
Accredidation: The Rutgers School of Public Health is accredited as a school of public health by the Council on Education for Public Health (CEPH), an independent agency recognized by the U.S. Department of Education to accredit schools of public health. [2, 3]

ProgramName: MPH in Occupational and Environmental Medicine
Requirements: Completion of the online application, official transcripts from all post-secondary institutions attended, a statement of goals (one-to-three pages), and two letters of recommendation are required. [2] At least one letter of recommendation should be from an academic reference if you are currently enrolled in a degree program or have graduated within the last four years. [2] A TOEFL or IELTS score is also necessary for applicants who were educated in a non-native English-speaking country. [2]
Description: The Rutgers School of Public Health's Master of Public Health (MPH) in Occupational and Environmental Medicine degree is designed to educate health care workers and physician trainees in the relevant health problems, policies, programs, and regulations that contribute to an individual's health by understanding and learning how to manage and prevent illness and injury caused or influenced by agents in the home, community, and workplace environment. [2] Graduates will be able to identify, articulate, and remedy workplace occupational safety and health issues, including exposure risks and their effects on workers, the general public, and vulnerable communities. [2] Graduates will also be well-trained in toxicology and dose-response, federal and state regulatory standards, and environmental factors that impact health outcomes. [2] Graduates are eligible to sit for the Certified in Public Health Exam. [2]
Accredidation: The Rutgers School of Public Health is accredited as a school of public health by the Council on Education for Public Health (CEPH), an independent agency recognized by the U.S. Department of Education to accredit schools of public health. [10]

ProgramName: MPH in Occupational Safety and Health
Requirements: A complete application includes: Completion of the online application; Official transcripts from all post-secondary institutions attended; Statement of goals, one-to-three pages in length, which addresses: Interest in the program, Preparedness for the program, Goals and aspirations; Two letters of recommendation with at least one letter from an academic reference if you are currently enrolled in a degree program or have graduated within the last four years; Resume or CV; GRE General Exam (optional); TOEFL or IELTS score for applicants educated in a non-native English-speaking country. [8]
Description: The Rutgers School of Public Health's Master of Public Health (MPH) in Occupational Safety and Health degree is dedicated to training professionals in the fundamentals of safety science, preparing graduates to mitigate workplace risks. Students will be trained to identify occupational safety and health issues in the workplace with specific coursework that will educate students on how to develop testable models to validate occupational exposures and adverse health outcomes and utilize their understanding of regulatory compliance standards to devise best-in-class solutions to ensure worker safety and health protection.
Accredidation: The Rutgers School of Public Health is accredited as a school of public health by the Council on Education for Public Health (CEPH), an independent agency recognized by the U.S. Department of Education to accredit schools of public health. [3]

ProgramName: MPH in Population Aging
Requirements: A complete application includes: Completion of the online application, a Statement of goals, one-to-three pages in length, which addresses: Interest in the program, Preparedness for the program, and Goals and aspirations, and Two letters of recommendation with at least one letter from an academic reference if you are currently enrolled in a degree program or have graduated within the last four years. [15]
Fees: $1,300.00/Credit (In-State)
Description: The Rutgers School of Public Health's fully online Master of Public Health (MPH) in Population Aging degree is designed to train scholars, clinicians, advocates, and community leaders in public health approaches to understanding, analyzing, and improving the health outcomes of older adults – the fastest growing segment of the United States population. [1] Students in this program will learn about the public health interventions, policies, theories, and challenges relevant to older adults. The innovative courses that make up the program will also prepare graduates to develop and implement innovative public health research programs and identify novel policy solutions aimed at improving older adults' physical and mental health. [1]
Accredidation: The Rutgers School of Public Health is accredited by the Council on Education for Public Health (CEPH). [2]

ProgramName: MPH in Population Mental Health
Requirements: A complete application includes: Completion of the online application; Official transcripts from all post-secondary institutions attended; Statement of goals, one-to-three pages in length, which addresses: Interest in the program; Preparedness for the program; Goals and aspirations. Two letters of recommendation with at least one letter from an academic reference if you are currently enrolled in a degree program or have graduated within the last four years. Resume or CV; GRE General Exam (optional); TOEFL or IELTS score for applicants educated in a non-native English-speaking country. [1]
Description: The Rutgers School of Public Health's Master of Public Health (MPH) in Population Mental Health degree prepares students to address the current challenges in mental health practice and reduce the societal burden of emotional distress, mental illness, substance abuse, alcohol use, and suicide. [2, 3] Students will be able to identify biological, psychological, structural, socioeconomic, and sociocultural correlates of population mental health, as well as examine the relationship between stigma, mental health, and health inequity. [2, 3] Graduates will be able to positively impact mental health policy and provide multifaceted interventions and practices to improve mental health and achieve health equity. [3] Graduates are eligible to sit for the Certified in Public Health Exam. [3]
Accredidation: The Rutgers School of Public Health is accredited by the Council on Education for Public Health. [3]

ProgramName: MPH in Public Health Nutrition
Requirements: A complete application includes: Completion of the online application; Official transcripts from all post-secondary institutions attended; Statement of goals, one-to-three pages in length, which addresses: Interest in the program. [4]

Description: The Rutgers School of Public Health's Master of Public Health (MPH) in Public Health Nutrition degree prepares students to improve the nutrition and health of local and global populations. [3] In partnership with the Department of Clinical and Preventive Nutrition Sciences in the Rutgers School of Health Professionals, this program provides students with the in-depth training required to assess dietary needs and develop nutrition interventions. [3] Graduates will be prepared to uniquely serve the needs of various communities including analyzing local and global food systems, identifying the nutritional status of populations, and the relationships between diet, nutrition, and health outcomes. [3] Graduates are eligible to sit for the Certified in Public Health Exam. [3]
Accredidation: Graduates are eligible to sit for the Certified in Public Health Exam. [3] The Rutgers School of Public Health and the Rutgers School of Health Professions also offer an MPH in Public Health Nutrition degree and DI graduate certificate, preparing students to become registered dietitian nutritionists (RDNs). [3] This dual program allows students to take the RDN credentialing exam after completing or receiving the MPH in Public Health Nutrition degree and DI graduate certificate. [3]

MPH in Social and Behavioral Health Sciences
Requirements:

Description: Based on the foundation of behavioral science research, the Rutgers School of Public Health's Master of Public Health (MPH) in Social and Behavioral Health Sciences degree prepares students to understand the importance of individual behaviors in health decision making. [3] Students will be trained in public health policy and health behavior theories and models to assess diverse populations. Graduates will be able to design, implement, conduct, and evaluate health education programs to positively impact health behavior change, health promotion, and health outcomes for all people and populations. [2, 3] Graduates are eligible to sit for the Certified in Public Health Exam and Certified Health Education Specialist Exam. [3]
Accredidation: The Rutgers School of Public Health is accredited by the Council on Education for Public Health (CEPH). [2]

ScholarshipType: The School of Public Health offers tuition scholarships, with a focus on students from underrepresented backgrounds and those working in state and local public health programs. [26]

ProgramName: MPH in Social Work and Public Health
Requirements: Students interested in the MPH in Social Work and Public Health degree will be required to apply and be accepted to both the Rutgers School of Social Work and Rutgers School of Public Health separately. [2, 3] A complete application includes: Online application; Official transcripts from all post-secondary institutions attended; Statement of goals, one-to-three pages in length, which addresses: Interest in the program; Preparedness for the program; Goals and aspirations. Two letters of recommendation with at least one letter from an academic reference.

ProgramName: MPH in Urban Public Health
Requirements: While specific requirements vary by program, general application materials for most graduate programs at Rutgers include an online application, a $70 non-refundable application fee, one official transcript from each post-secondary institution attended, letters of recommendation as required by the program, and a personal statement. [2, 5] Some programs may also require test scores and other supporting materials. [2]
Description: The Rutgers School of Public Health's Master of Public Health (MPH) in Urban Public Health degree prepares students to advance health and well-being in diverse, dynamic, and often marginalized, urban populations in New Jersey, the United States, and the world. [2] Through in-depth training and coursework, graduates of the MPH in Urban Public Health degree have a thorough understanding of systems and structures that lead to inequities, the social determinants of health, and intervention planning that meets community needs. [2] As a result, graduates are able to collaborate with communities to positively impact health with a lens of equity and social justice. [2] Graduates are eligible to sit for the Certified in Public Health Exam. [2]
Accredidation: CEPH Accreditation. [2]
CostPerCredit: $1,083 per credit (in-state), $1,620 per credit (out-of-state) for the 2025-2026 academic year

ProgramName: MS in Biostatistics
Requirements: A complete application includes: Online application, Official transcripts from all post-secondary institutions attended, Statement of goals, one-to-three pages in length, which addresses: Interest in the program, Preparedness for the program, and Goals and aspirations, and Two letters of recommendation with at least one letter from an academic reference if you have graduated within the last four years.
Description: The MS in Biostatistics degree, a STEM designated program, prepares students to possess the knowledge and technical skills needed for the design, data analysis, and interpretation of findings from modern health-related studies. Students enrolled in the program will learn about statistical theory and modeling, as well as gain real experience utilizing a variety of statistical software packages that enable them to design and analyze data from experimental and observational data sets, to help solve medical and public health problems, and to communicate findings to investigators or community members. [12] The objectives of the M.S. in biostatistics neuralgiare: (1) to educate graduate students as biostatisticians at the master's level with the ability to collaborate and consult with researchers of other disciplines in the biomedical and public health sciences; (2) to meet the need for well-trained master's-level biostatisticians for the pharmaceutical industry, medical research institutions, and public health and other governmental organizations in New Jersey and nationwide; and (3) to identify and educate promising doctoral students in biostatistics. [10]
CostPerCredit: $1,083/credit (Resident), $1,620/credit (Non-Resident)

ProgramName: MS in Epidemiology (Pharmacoepidemiology Option)
Requirements:
While programs may require additional materials, here are the basic application requirements:

* Online application
* $70 nonrefundable application fee
* One official transcript from each post-secondary institution attended
* Letters of recommendation, as required by the program
* A personal statement

* Supporting materials, as required by the program. [2]
Description: The research-based MS degree in Epidemiology, Pharmacoepidemiology Concentration, provides students with critically important, in-depth training to bridge the gaps between epidemiology, pharmaceutical science, therapeutics, and population health. [4] Students will learn how to select and implement pharmacoepidemiologic techniques to quantitatively evaluate patterns and changes in disease and treatment of disease. [4] To ensure high quality standard of care and treatment patterns, students will also study how to assess medicinal use benefits and detriments through pharmacoepidemiologic research and practice. [4] The master of science (M.S.) degree in epidemiology is designed to equip students with comprehensive knowledge and skills in epidemiological research and methodology. [6] The objectives of the M.S. in epidemiology are to: (1) prepare graduates to collaborate and consult as epidemiologists across various disciplines in the biomedical, clinical, and public health sectors; (2) address the increasing demand for master's-level epidemiologists in healthcare, governmental, and non-governmental organizations, as well as in the pharmaceutical and research industries; and (3) identify and mentor promising students for advanced doctoral training in epidemiology. [6]

ProgramName: MS in Health Outcomes, Policy, & Economics
Requirements: The Master of Science in Health Outcomes, Policy, and Economics (MS-HOPE) is jointly offered by the Ernest Mario School of Pharmacy and the School of Public Health. [3] The curriculum includes coursework in health economics, biostatistics, health care policy and financing, and clinical research design. [3] Students are required to complete a two-semester Capstone Project. [3] The program requires the completion of 30 credit hours, a qualifying examination, and a research paper. [3] For the dual-degree PharmD/MS-HOPE program, applicants must be enrolled in the Ernest Mario School of Pharmacy PharmD program with a cumulative professional GPA of 3.2 or higher. [4] Applications are submitted through the School of Public Health Admissions System (SOPHAS). [4]
Description: The Master of Science in Health Outcomes, Policy and Economics (MS-HOPE) provides premier education and research on the effectiveness and costs of healthcare innovations, such as pharmaceuticals and devices. [1] Coursework focuses on epidemiology, outcomes research, biocomputing, health economics, and health policy. [1]
Accredidation: The Rutgers School of Public Health, which offers the MS in Health Outcomes, Policy, & Economics, is accredited by the Council on Education for Public Health (CEPH).

ProgramName: PhD in Public Health (Concentration in Biostatistics and Epidemiology)
Requirements: Requirements for admission to the PhD program are generally more stringent than those for the MPH or MS degree programs. Considerable attention is given to the match between the expertise of the faculty and the specific interests of the candidate. Each applicant to the PhD progra is required to submit a full application, including identification of an area of proposed research. These materials will be reviewed by the entire doctoral committee for quality and compatibility with the interests of the faculty.

ProgramName: PhD in Public Health (Concentration in Environmental and Occupational Health)
Requirements: For the PhD in Public Health, a master's degree in public health (MPH) from a CEPH-accredited school or program is preferred, but not required. Applicants without an MPH will need to complete the MPH core curriculum. A bachelor's degree is required.
Department: Rutgers School of Public Health and Rutgers School of Graduate Studies
Description: The Rutgers School of Public Health and Rutgers School of Graduate Studies' rigorous PhD in Public Health degree is designed to support public health professionals seeking a research-based graduate program, offering advanced study across five concentration areas. [7] This webpage provides details on the PhD in Public Health (Environmental and Occupational Health). [7] Upon graduation, a student completing the PhD in Public Health curriculum in Environmental and Occupational Health will be able to: PhD-ENOH1: Conduct an environmental and occupational health literature review across the exposure-disease continuum, assess its strengths and weaknesses, and identify knowledge gaps and future research directions. [7]
CostPerCredit: $1,083 per credit for in-state students and $1,620 per credit for out-of-state students (2025-2026 academic year)
MaxFails: no more than nine (9) credits bearing grades less than B
ScholarshipType: Fellowships, research assistantships, and teaching assistantships

ProgramName: PhD in Public Health (Concentrations in Social and Behavioral Health Sciences or Health Systems and Policy)
Requirements: The PhD in Public Health is a full-time program. Students seeking the PhD in Public Health-Social & Behavioral Health Sciences degree must complete a minimum of 72 credits of academic work with a minimum GPA of at least 3.2 overall and a 3.2 in the set of required courses specified by the concentration. [19] Students in the Health Systems & Policy concentration must also complete a minimum of 72 credits with a minimum GPA of 3.2. [17] Each applicant must submit a full application. [14]
Department: Rutgers School of Public Health and Rutgers School of Graduate Studies
Concentration: ['Social and Behavioral Health Sciences', 'Health Systems and Policy']
Description: The Doctor of Philosophy in Public Health prepares students for careers in research and/or academia. [14] Through doctoral level training and research, students will develop expertise in a particular concentration area, design and implement a research project, integrate and interpret complex data, and complete a comprehensive dissertation. [14] For the advancement of health, wellness, and prevention of disease, our Public Health doctoral students continuously produce scholarly research in one of five concentration areas: biostatistics, environmental and occupational health, epidemiology, health systems and policy, and social and behavioral health sciences. [14] This program, offered through a partnership between the Rutgers School of Public Health and the Rutgers School of Graduate Studies, is designed for public health professionals seeking a research-based graduate program. [2]
MinimumTOEFLScore: Writing 22, Speaking 23, Reading 21, Listening 17 for iBT; 550 for paper-based

ProgramName: DrPH in Leadership, Practice, and Research
Requirements: Applicants for admission must have earned a master's degree from an accredited program in the United States or its equivalent and must have demonstrated academic achievement in an appropriate discipline. [1, 2] In addition, applicants must have a minimum of five years of professional experience within a public health or health-related setting. [1, 2] The following must be submitted: Official transcripts of all prior academic work, a Letter of Intent, and three letters of recommendation. [2] The Letter of Intent should address why the DrPH is of interest at this stage of their career, the key knowledge and skills they hope to gain from the program, and how the degree will help to advance their leadership in the field of public health. [2] Students who have graduated from an institution outside of the United States must have an official course-by-course evaluation of foreign transcripts through World Education Services (WES) and submit a Test of English as a Foreign Language (TOEFL) score. [2] If a student does not have a Master of Public Health degree from a Council on Education for Public Health-accredited school, they will be required to complete the Post-Baccalaureate Certificate in Population Health coursework. [1, 2]
Description: The Rutgers School of Public Health's Doctor of Public Health (DrPH) in Leadership, Practice, and Research degree prepares mid- to senior-career professionals to assume positions of greater responsibility and to achieve public health impact at local, state, national, and/or international levels by increasing a student's practical knowledge of theory and public health training while honing their leadership, practice, and research skill sets. [2]
Accredidation: A student who does not have a Master of Public Health degree from a Council on Education for Public Health-accredited school or program of public health, will be required to complete the Post-Baccalaureate Certificate in Population Health coursework. [1]
MaxFails: Students may earn no more than nine (9) credits bearing grades less than B. [1]

ProgramName: Concentration in Neuroscience

[11] Students will be able to: Understand the essential properties of neural cells as they relate to their functions. [11] Understand the anatomy of the nervous system and how each division alone and in conjunction with other divisions coordinates neural functions. [11] Understand how to apply the research tools of modern biomedical science to neuroscience. [11] Acquire the knowledge required to understand the molecular and cellular bases for neurological and psychiatric diseases and their treatment. [11]

[1] Students will have the opportunity to: understand the properties of pathogenic and commensal bacteria in oral health and disease; understand the immune system's role in oral health and pathology; understand physiological concepts and their application to clinical dentistry; understand human biochemistry with an emphasis on dental problems; understand structure-function relationships and their correlations with clinical dentistry; understand the principles of material science and biomaterials; understand sensory systems in the oral cavity; and understand modern dental-related biomedical science research techniques. [1]

ProgramName: Concentration in Pharmacological Sciences
Department: School of Graduate Studies, Newark Health Science Campus

Description: The Concentration in Pharmacological Sciences is designed for students who wish to gain a focused area of knowledge without committing to a full master's degree, though it can be taken as part of a Master's program. [3, 8] It is geared towards individuals aiming for careers in the pharmaceutical or biotechnology industries, teaching, journalism, or administration. [3] To earn the concentration, students are required to complete the "PHPY 5021 Fundamentals of Pharmacology" course and two out of six elective courses, totaling 8 or 9 credits. [2] The curriculum covers the quantitative aspects of dose-effect relationships, drug antagonism, and specificity. [2, 5] Elective topics include central nervous system disorders, endocrine clinical problems, chemotherapy, toxicology, and the business of drug discovery and development from discovery to market. [2, 5] The program provides a strong foundation in pharmacokinetics, pharmacodynamics, drug development, clinical trials, and regulation. [8]

ProgramName: Concentration in Stem Cell Biology
Requirements: While programs may require additional materials, the basic application requirements are: an online application, a $70 nonrefundable application fee, one official transcript from each post-secondary institution attended, three letters of recommendation, a personal statement, and current test results as required by the program. [5]
Department: School of Graduate Studies (SGS) - Newark Health Science Campus
Description: All students must complete the required course (MSBS 5130Q) and take any two of the four offered elective courses. This will be a total of 7 credits to earn the Stem Cell Biology concentration. If you were not able to take MSBS 5130 Stem Cell Biology and Applications in Molecular Medicine in fall 2023, please contact the concentration coordinator, Dr. Doreen Badheka (doreen.badheka@rutgers.edu) for updated concentration requirements. [1]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Accounting
Requirements: Application and Self-Reported Academic Record (SRAR).
Description: The program in accounting a a comprehensive foundation in the theory of accounting, financial accounting and reporting, managerial and cost accounting, taxation, concepts of auditing, and business law. It is built on a broad background in humanities, liberal arts, economics, and business administration. The accounting program gives students the foundation and skills to pursue careers with public accounting firms, corporations, government, and nonprofit organizations. The program provides the background to sit for the Certified Public Accountant (C.P.A.), Certified Management Accountant (C.M.A.), and Certified Internal Auditor (C.I.A.) examinations. Graduates of this program can also pursue further graduate or professional education. [2]
Accredidation: Rutgers Business School earned AACSB International accreditation in 1941 (then named the School of Business Administration) and has maintained accreditation through every review since. [6, 9]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Aerospace Engineering
Description: The aerospace engineering program at Rutgers provides a broad and multi-disciplinary education in the fundamentals of aircraft and spacecraft design. Rutgers is currently the only public university in New Jersey offering an aerospace engineering degree. The program offers multiple degree options for students, including: a BS and a BS/MS Five-Year Dual Degree. The department also offers an energy systems concentration. Students completing the requirements for this concentration receive a certificate in addition to their aerospace engineering diploma. Unmanned aerial systems, airplane and space vehicle design, propulsion, flight technology, aerodynamics and astrodynamics, aerospace materials and structures, aerospace modeling and simulations, and sensing and control of aerospace systems are all components of our aerospace engineering degree.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in African, Middle Eastern, and South Asian Languages and Literatures
Requirements: First-year applicants should submit the application and a Self-Reported Academic Record (SRAR). An official high school transcript will be required.
Department: Department of African, Middle Eastern, and South Asian Languages and Literatures (AMESALL)
Description: The Major in African, Middle Eastern and South Asian Languages and Literatures is open to students admitted to and enrolled in any of the campuses and schools at Rutgers-New Brunswick. The Major requires two years of language study (or the equivalent proficiency) as a prerequisite, and the successful completion of at least 33 credit hours. It has two options, a Global Humanities option and a Regional option. [2] With a Bachelor of Arts in African, Middle Eastern, and South Asian Languages and Literatures, you will acquire an advanced level of proficiency in any one of these languages and explore their rich and vibrant literary and cultural traditions from ancient times to the 21st century. [1] The program teaches the languages and literatures of Africa, the Middle East, and South Asia. [3] Students can discover the mystical love poetry of Persia, the magical world of African folklore and myth, the magnificent Vedic scriptures of India, and the controversial modern fiction of Nobel-prize winning authors from the three regions. [1] AMESALL prepares students for graduate school and a range of professional or academic degrees, or for the challenges of the job market in a globalized world. [1]
Accredidation: Middle States Accreditation [12]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Africana Studies
Description: The Bachelor of Arts in Africana Studies offers a comprehensive exploration of African and African diasporic experiences. This program prepares students to understand the complexities of culture, history, and social dynamics through an interdisciplinary framework. You'll engage with various disciplines, including history, sociology, and literature, enhancing your critical thinking and analytical skills. Classes typically focus on contemporary issues and historical contexts related to Africana studies.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in American Studies
Requirements: Rutgers reviews a comprehensive set of factors for admission, including academic performance and the completion of a self-reported academic record. Application is through the Rutgers application or the Common App. For a complete list of required high school coursework (16 academic units), applicants should refer to the university's official admissions website.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Animal Science
Requirements: To enroll in the School of Environmental and Biological Sciences, the home of the Animal Science major, you must apply through Rutgers Undergraduate Admissions. First-year entrance requirements include: 4 years of English, 3 years of mathematics (including algebra I, geometry, and algebra II), and 2 years of science, for a total of 16 academic courses. Other factors considered include the quality of the academic program, class rank, and extracurricular activities. [2]
Department: School of Environmental and Biological Sciences

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Anthropology
Requirements: First-year applicants must submit an online application, pay a nonrefundable application fee, and complete the Self-Reported Academic Record (SRAR).
Concentration: ['B.A. Track in Anthropology', 'B.A. Track in Cultural Anthropology', 'B.S. in Evolutionary Anthropology']
Description: The B.A. track in anthropology trains students in the discipline's four traditional subfields: cultural, biological, and linguistic anthropology and archaeology, providing them with a holistic understanding of humans as biological, cultural, and linguistic beings, both in the present and the past. This track is intended for students who seek a comprehensive understanding of human cultural and physical diversity within a broad social, historical, and evolutionary framework. [5, 9] The department's work is organized through two broad intellectual tracks: CITE (Critical Interventions in Theory and Ethnography), which encompasses Cultural, Linguistic, and Medical Anthropology, and HES (Human Evolutionary Sciences), which includes Primatology, Human Behavioral Ecology, Biological Anthropology, and Archaeology. [2] The curriculum provides tools for observation, investigation, and research, helping to foster the ability to formulate new hypotheses and communicate new discoveries. [3]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Anthropology
Requirements: Rutgers University does not offer a specific degree named 'Bachelor of Science in Anthropology'. They offer a Bachelor of Arts in Anthropology. For a first-year application to Rutgers, in general, you need to submit a self-reported academic record, and you have the option to submit ACT/SAT scores and a personal essay.
ScholarshipAmount: The Carr Scholarship provides $10,000 per year, and the Chancellor's Scholarship can range up to $5,000 per year. Other endowed scholarships range from $500–$5,000 per year. [26]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Art
Requirements: Prospective Rutgers students who are interested only in the BA Art degree (and not any BFA degree) do not need to complete this application process. Only current Rutgers may apply for BA Art. Applicants will submit the MGSA BA in Art Interest Form by February 1 and complete a Talent Assessment for approval by February 15 for priority consideration. [15]
Department: Mason Gross School of the Arts
Fees: For the 2024-2025 academic year, full-time tuition at the Mason Gross School of the Arts is $15,984.00 per year for New Jersey residents and $37,876.00 per year for out-of-state residents. These figures are based on the per-semester rates and are subject to change.
Description: The Bachelor of Arts (B.A.) program in visual arts at Rutgers University's Mason Gross School of the Arts allows students to explore the materials, techniques, places, events, and images that form the basis for understanding the artist's position in the modern world. The program emphasizes the fundamental principles of visual arts in both studio courses and art history. All undergraduate students in the Department of Art & Design begin with the same foundation studio curriculum to familiarize them with core concepts and basic skills. The curriculum includes the study of drawing, color, and composition, as well as the exploration of spatial dynamics and temporal qualities, while encouraging experimentation and critical inquiry. Students in the BA track are not required to declare a concentration; instead, they pursue more liberal arts requirements within the wider university.
CostPerCredit: For the 2024-2025 academic year, the part-time tuition rate for New Jersey residents at the Mason Gross School of the Arts is $525.00 per credit, and for out-of-state residents, it is $1,262.00 per credit. These rates are subject to change.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Fine Arts in Art

Following the submission of the university application, applicants will receive a link to complete the Mason Gross Talent Assessment. This assessment includes a $25 fee, an Art & Design Questionnaire, a Personal Statement, and a portfolio. The portfolio should consist of 15-20 examples of artwork created within the last two years. [2]
Department: Mason Gross School of the Arts
Concentration: For the BFA in visual arts, students choose a concentration in one of six areas: drawing, media, painting, photography, print, and sculpture. Students may opt to double concentrate or do a hybrid concentration with approval by two faculty members and guidance of the undergraduate advisor. [9]
Description: Foundation courses introduce the techniques and materials as well as the artistic and cultural questions nutty professor of contemporary practice. Intermediate and advanced courses provide specific training in the area of concentration: design, drawing, media, painting, photography, print or sculpture. Studies culminate in the final year BFA thesis exhibition in the Mason Gross Galleries. [9]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Art History
Requirements: For first-year applicants, Rutgers conducts a holistic review of the application, which includes academic performance, a personal essay, and extracurricular activities. [9] Applicants are required to submit a completed application via the Rutgers Application or the Common App and, if a current high school senior, must complete a Self-reported Transcript and Academic Record System (STARS) Record. [9] Minimum high school coursework includes 16 academic units: 4 years of English, 3 years of math (Algebra I, Geometry, Algebra II), 2 years of a foreign language, 2 years of science, and 5 other academic courses. [8]
Description: Studying art history offers a fascinating look at the world through visual arts, and enables you to interpret the work of many cultures and eras through architecture, paintings, and sculpture. Courses taught by internationally recognized faculty cover both European American and wider global traditions including Islamic, Latin American, African and Asian art. [25] You will gain excellent preparation for graduate study, after which you can consider becoming a curator for a major museum or director of an art gallery. [25] Some graduates move on to law school to apply their skills in the growing field of litigation involving works of art. Many employers in businesses ranging from internet start-ups to advertising seek people who know how to look carefully and think visually, which is the core of what our program teaches. [25]

Description: The Astrophysics Major, leading to a Bachelor of Science degree, provides a thorough introduction to the subject. It is suitable for those with an interest in astronomy who aspire to a career in astronomy research, science education, science journalism, technical development, and other professional areas. ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Biochemistry

The curriculum has four components: the Life Sciences Core Curriculum, the Chemistry Core Curriculum, MBB Curricular Options courses, and MBB Independent Research. For the MBB Curricular Options, students must choose either the 'Electives' Option, for those with broad interests in the field, or the 'P-Chem' Option, for students with a strong background in math who may be pursuing research and graduate work in the physical biosciences. [1] The program prepares students for graduate studies in molecular biology and biochemistry and related fields, entry into professional schools in medicine or other health professions, or employment in industries like biotechnology and pharmaceuticals.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Bioengineering and Biomedical Engineering
Requirements: For admission to the School of Engineering, where the Bioengineering and Biomedical Engineering program resides, your high school record must show that you will graduate or have graduated with at least 16 academic units. [2] This includes 4 years of English, 4 years of Mathematics (including algebra I, geometry, algebra II, and pre-calculus or calculus), 1 year of Chemistry, and 1 year of Physics. [2] Applicants must complete either the Common App or the Rutgers Application and submit a Self-reported Transcript and Academic Record System (STARS) Record. [4, 9] High school seniors apply to the School of Engineering and declare an engineering major, such as Biomedical Engineering, in the spring of their first year. [16]
Concentration: ['Biomechanics and Rehabilitation Engineering', 'Biomedical Computing, Imaging, and Instrumentation', 'Tissue Engineering and Molecular Bioengineering']
Description: A biomedical engineer brings together traditional engineering principals with the life sciences in a completely integrated fashion. The result is an engineer who views the human body as a complex system, its diseases and injuries as breakdowns in that system, and medical interventions as design alternatives for the repair of the system. [2]
Accredidation: The B.S. program in Biomedical Engineering is accredited by the Engineering Accreditation Commission of ABET, http://www.abet.org.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Biological Sciences

Description: The biological sciences major is the largest in the School of Arts and Sciences and is administered by the Division of Life Sciences. Students take a two-semester sequence of introductory biology, a one-semester course in genetics, and then select five advanced courses from a wide range of topics that reflect the breadth of the biological sciences. The major is available as both a bachelor of arts (B.A.) and a bachelor of science (B.S.) degree. The biological sciences major is excellent preparation for a career in medicine and other health professions, teaching, research, and for positions in the biotechnology and pharmaceutical industries. A student majoring in biological sciences at Rutgers can choose from a wide variety of courses, including molecular biology and biochemistry, organismal biology, and ecology and evolution. These can be combined with a wide variety of advanced-level courses in any area of interest, and supplemented by research with a faculty member. [3, 6, 9]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Biological Sciences

Description: The major in Biological Sciences, administered through the Division of Life Sciences Office of Undergraduate Instruction, is intended to provide a broad and comprehensive training in modern biology. This course of study is recommended for those who wish to study biology as part of their liberal arts education, preparing them for a career in one of the health professions, graduate studies in biology, a teaching career in secondary schools (courses in education are also required), as well as employment in various areas of the life sciences. [9] The Bachelor of Science (B.S.) degree in biology requires 38 credits of coursework in biological sciences, plus cognate courses in chemistry, physics, and mathematics. [2] The major can be completed only by daytime attendance. [4]
Accredidation: Rutgers University is accredited by the Middle States Commission on Higher Education. [16] The American Society for Biochemistry and Molecular Biology (ASBMB) also lists Rutgers University as having an accredited program. [21]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Biotechnology
Requirements: Rutgers conducts a holistic review of each student's application. Primary emphasis is placed on academic promise as demonstrated by completion of required high school subjects, academic performance in high school (including strength of program, grades, and grade trends), and cumulative rank if available. Rutgers also considers the personal essay, participation in college preparation programs, extracurricular activities, community service, U.S. military service, honors and awards, and employment history. [20]

Description: The curriculum in biotechnology provides the student with fundamental knowledge and laboratory skills in biotechnology, with focus areas in molecular biology, genetics, genomics, proteomics, bioinformatics, and delivery/formulation technologies. These are underpinned by a firm foundation in biology and the physical sciences. The primary objectives of the program are to broadly educate students for positions in the biotechnology industry and/or to prepare students for graduate and professional study in the life sciences. Training in the Undergraduate Program in Biotechnology is centered in applied genetics, biochemistry and molecular biology with options to focus in various application areas. The curriculum includes lab-based courses in molecular genetics, genetic engineering, genomics, proteomics, bioinformatics, microbiology, biochemistry and others with applications in medicine, biopharmaceutics, agriculture and environmental mediation.
ScholarshipType: The School of Environmental and Biological Sciences (SEBS) offers school-specific scholarships. The university also offers merit-based and need-based scholarships.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Business Administration

Description: The Rutgers bachelor of arts in business administration (B.B.A.) program delivers a cutting-edge curriculum taught by exceptional faculty. Depending on a student's work or life schedule, this program is designed so that the student can balance responsibilities and complete the degree program at their own pace. Courses are offered in fall, winter, spring, and summer.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Cell Biology and Neuroscience
Requirements: Application requirements for first-year students at Rutgers University are not detailed on a single page for the 'Bachelor of Science in Cell Biology and Neuroscience' program. Applicants are expected to follow the general first-year application process, which includes submission of a self-reported academic record, and for some programs, a portfolio or an audition. Standardized test scores are optional.
Description: The Cell Biology and Neuroscience major provides an exciting and challenging academic environment by combining excellence in research with a strong commitment to undergraduate and graduate education. The program's research encompasses the complementary areas of cell biology, developmental biology, and neurobiology with an emphasis on fundamental problems in cell signaling and communication. [6] Students can study the role of cellular defects in neurodegenerative disorders such as Alzheimer's, or investigate brain activity dynamics underlying learning and decision-making. [2] The curriculum includes introductory lecture courses to build a strong foundation, advanced courses on current scientific developments, hands-on laboratory coursework, and research opportunities. [6]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Chemistry

Description: The Bachelor of Arts in Chemistry program prepares graduates interested in science-oriented pre-professional programs such as medicine and dentistry, as well as for students entering secondary science teaching. The B.A. program allows students to major with a maximum of forty-six credits in chemistry while provides flexibility for exposure in other cognate fields. ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Chemistry

A certain core of courses is required for completion of the major in chemistry. Included is coursework in the four major subdisciplines of chemistry--inorganic, organic, physical, and analytical--as well as work in mathematics and physics. [17] The curriculum is designed to permit the student a wide range of career choices, including, but not limited to, chemistry, medicine, law, business, chemical physics, environmental science, and secondary school teaching. Four courses in Chinese literature, history, and/or culture (under subject code 165). One course chosen from East Asian Civilizations: Traditional Era (098:241) OR East Asian Civilizations: Modern Era (098:242) OR Global East Asia (098:250). Capstone Seminar on East Asian Studies (098:444).

[3] The university conducts a holistic review of each application. [7] While not a specific requirement for the Cinema Studies program itself, the general Rutgers application includes an essay. [4]
Description: Cinema Studies is an interdisciplinary program where you will gain an understanding of the technical aspects of filmmaking; learn about the historical development of the film medium from the earliest days of silent cinema to the most recent advances in digital production; study questions of narrative and genre; and explore the relationship between culture, politics, and moving image media, through the analysis of films produced around the globe and across more than a century. [11]
CostPerCredit: New Jersey resident $482 per credit; Non-New Jersey resident $1,162 per credit. [27]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Cognitive Science
Requirements: First-year applicants are admitted to the School of Arts and Sciences and declare their major at a later time. The university conducts a holistic review of each student's application, considering academic strength and performance, the essay, and extracurricular activities. [17] To declare a major in Cognitive Science, students must complete specific prerequisite courses in Computational/Logical Reasoning, Statistical Reasoning, and Introduction to Cognitive Science with a grade of C or better. [10, 16]
Fees: The tuition for the School of Arts and Sciences is listed as $14,933 for New Jersey residents for the academic year. [24] For out-of-state students, the cost per credit is $1,162. [24]
Description: Cognitive Science is an interdisciplinary area of scholarship concerned with understanding the nature and development of perception, language, reasoning, planning, problem-solving, and related skills in biological or artificial systems. [12] It investigates perception, action, language, knowledge, development, and thinking from multiple perspectives—theoretical, experimental, and computational—with the aim of gaining a better understanding of human cognition and the nature of intelligent systems. [5] The major will make it possible for students to cultivate unique interests within cognitive science by allowing them to create novel course combinations that transcend the typical departmental boundaries. [5] The field spans a wide variety of disciplines including computer science, linguistics, mathematics, neuroscience, philosophy, and psychology. [8]
CostPerCredit: $482/credit hour for in-state residents
ScholarshipAmount: Scholarships can range from $5,000 to $16,000 per year, with specific awards like the Carr Scholarship valued at $10,000 annually.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Communication
Requirements: Admission to the Communication major is selective. To apply, students must have completed at least 15 credits at Rutgers (or have at least 15 transfer credits) with a minimum 2.0 GPA. Required prerequisite courses include College Writing (01:355:101) or equivalent, and Introduction to Communication and Information Processes (04:189:101), both with a grade of C or better. [11, 13, 15] Admission is not open to first-year students; they must first enroll in a separate Rutgers undergraduate school. [13] The application includes a one-page essay about interest in the major and post-graduation plans. [13]
Concentration: ['Health and Wellness Communication', 'Leadership in Organizations and Community', 'Relationship and Family Communication', 'Strategic Public Communication and Public Relations', 'Communication and Technology']
Description: The Communication major at Rutgers offers a theoretically-oriented investigation of how discourses, communication systems, media institutions, built environments, and human activity together shape economic, political, and cultural life. The program's interdisciplinary curriculum is rich in hands-on learning opportunities for students interested in designing and producing media, conducting fieldwork, and bridging social divides through participation at faculty directed, regional community sites. Students are taught a wide variety of reading and research methods, including qualitative data collection, textual analysis, historical research, critical theory, intersectionality, and discourse analysis. This means students will learn how to interpret and analyze media texts, read and decode digital publications and data, evaluate the role of technology and social change in cultural production, and critique representations of social reality in relation to power differentials, systemic stereotyping, and historical erasures. The courses also provide students space to engage in informed, reflective, and mindful dialogue about difficult social issues, confronting subjects such as race, gender, sexuality, class, policing, and war. Graduates complete the Communication major with a solid liberal arts background necessary for graduate studies in communication and many other disciplines, and for professional work in a number of communication- and media-related fields, including primary and secondary education.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Comparative Literature
Fees: Tuition: $14,933, Fees: $3,891 for the 2025-2026 academic year for New Jersey Residents in the School of Arts and Sciences–New Brunswick. [19]
Concentration: ['Comparative Literary Studies (CLS)', 'Colonial and Postcolonial Studies (CPS)', 'Cultural Theories and Practices (CTP)', 'Advanced Studies in Comparative Literature']
Description: Comparative Literature is the interdisciplinary study of global literary and cultural expressions as they shape and are shaped by science, economics, religion, politics, law, sexuality, media, and other historical forces. [17] The discipline and our program attract students with wide-ranging interests in literature, theory, cultural and media studies, and who wish to read literature in the original language as well as in translation. [17] Comp Lit considers texts and performances across time, space, languages, disciplines, and media. [1] Our students construct a unique course of literary, linguistic, and cultural study with the supervision and support of our distinguished international faculty. [1, 10] Students who speak languages in addition to English find our program an especially congenial place in which to read, watch, think, and create. [10] Students craft, in close consultation with the Director of Undergraduate Studies, a personalized major that best represents each student's research interests. [17]
CostPerCredit: $482/credit hour for the School of Arts and Sciences

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Computer Science

Core courses provide a foundation for all students in programming languages, data structures, software engineering, computer architectures, the theory of computation, the basics of building secure software and systems, teaming and communication, and the social and ethical dimensions of the practice of computer science. [18]
