ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Criminal Justice
Description: The Bachelor of Arts in Criminal Justice program provides students with a comprehensive understanding of crime, the criminal justice system, and the societal response to crime. The curriculum is interdisciplinary, drawing from fields like sociology, law, psychology, and political science. Students in the program explore the causes of crime, the functions of the police, courts, and correctional systems, and the legal and ethical issues in criminal justice. The program aims to develop critical thinking, research skills, and a strong foundation for careers in law enforcement, corrections, court services, social services, and for advanced studies in law or graduate school.
CostPerCredit: $482 per credit (NJ resident); $1,162 per credit (Non-NJ resident)

ProgramName: Bachelor of Fine Arts in Dance
Requirements: To be considered for admission to the BFA in Dance program, applicants must submit a Rutgers University Application and a Mason Gross Supplemental Application. [15] The supplemental application includes a dance audition fee, a dance questionnaire, a resume and headshot, and a recorded audition video. [15] An audition is required for all applicants to the dance department at the Mason Gross School of the Arts. [11] Students applying to the BFA in dance must submit an application to the Mason Gross School of the Arts and participate in an audition. [6]
Department: Mason Gross School of the Arts
Fees: The Rutgers website provides tuition and fee information for the 2025-2026 academic year, which can serve as an estimate. These costs vary based on the school or college and a student's personal choices. [14]
Description: The Bachelor of Fine Arts in Dance degree program is for students seeking careers as professional dance artists. [2] Students pursue their goals within the artistic and intellectual climate of a major research university and work with a diverse group of accomplished faculty who ensure expert direction in all three areas of the curriculum: performance and choreography, pedagogy, and dance theory. [2] Just 45 minutes from New York City, Mason Gross Dance enrolls a cohort of approximately 30-35 students each year in the BFA degree program. [2] BFA dance majors pursue their studies in a dedicated community that prioritizes their development as future artists, educators, and scholars. [2] Students are guided to extend and refine their artistic potential through work in multiple studios and performance facilities. [2] The Dance Department regularly hosts dance companies, dance practitioners, and scholars who are internationally renowned in the field, offering students opportunities to work side-by-side on the stage and in the classroom with professional choreographers, dance educators, and dance scholars. [2]
Accredidation: Nation Association of Schools of Dance (NASD) [1]
CostPerCredit: $482 per credit for New Jersey residents and $1,162 per credit for non-New Jersey residents (for the 2025–2026 academic year). [14]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Economics
Requirements: Prospective students apply to Rutgers University through a centralized admissions process. The primary requirements include the submission of a completed application and a Self-Reported Academic Record (SRAR).
Concentration: ['Financial Economics', 'Global Economics', 'Public Policy Economics', 'Economic Theory', 'Computational Data Analytics']
Description: The Bachelor of Arts in Economics helps students examine how society produces and consumes goods, and it analyzes many real-world issues such as international trade, poverty, taxes, crime, and education. [2] The curriculum provides students with thorough training in both theoretical and empirical approaches to real world problems, and it provides a framework in which to analyze human behavior. [2] In doing so, students graduate with the skills needed for successful careers in a wide range of fields including finance, consulting, accounting, and government. [2]
CostPerCredit: $482/credit hour

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Electrical and Electronics Engineering
Requirements: Required high school coursework includes: 4 years of English, 4 years of mathematics (including algebra I, geometry, algebra II, and pre-calculus or higher), 1 year of chemistry, and 1 year of physics. A total of 16 academic courses are required. It is recommended that students who complete pre-calculus before their senior year take calculus. Application is through the Common Application or the Rutgers Application, and requires the submission of a Self-Reported Academic Record (SRAR).
Description: The Rutgers electrical and computer engineering program is noted for its up-to-the-minute coursework and research opportunities in world-class labs in fields ranging from cloud computing, robotics, and digital signal processing to virtual reality and nanotechnology. The program offers two curriculum options, allowing students to focus their coursework and electives in either electrical engineering or computer engineering. A foundation in Electrical and Computer Engineering fundamentals is provided through courses in linear systems, electronic devices and circuits, digital signal processing, communications engineering, logic design, computer architecture, computer graphics and vision, Internet of Things, robotics, and virtual reality technology. [11] The electrical engineering option is designed to provide expertise in areas such as wireless communication systems and networks, signal and information processing, information privacy and security, cyberphysical systems, electronic materials, devices and circuits, biosensors, bio-electrical engineering, computer vision, and robotics. The computer engineering option prepares students for careers in computer hardware and software engineering, software verification, embedded systems, FPGA, human-computer interaction, cloud computing, and virtual reality, building upon a broad background in electrical engineering. [4]
Accredidation: The undergraduate program in Electrical and Computer Engineering is accredited by the Engineering Accreditation Commission of ABET. [3, 7, 8, 13]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in English

Description: English is a dynamic, evolving field, always committed to the reexamination of older traditions and the exploration of newer ones. You will gain both historical and critical skills through an inventive array of course electives and specialized options. Our English program is regularly ranked among the top 20 programs in the United States, and our English faculty are active leaders and participants in many of the university's strongest interdisciplinary centers, including the Center for Cultural Analysis, the Center for Historical Analysis, and the Institute for Research on Women. Our department is committed to excellence in written expression, to the interdisciplinary study of culture, and to the promotion of creative writing and multimedia composition. [14]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Exercise Science and Sport Studies
Requirements: To be admitted to the science program, students must have a cumulative grade-point average of at least 2.0 and have completed both General Biology courses (01:199:101-102) and Basic Statistics for Exercise Science (01:377:275) or its equivalent with a grade of C or better. [11] An interview with the department is required prior to admission to the program. [11] Students who wish to declare a major in Exercise Science or Sport Management must have completed a minimum of 1 semester at Rutgers University-New Brunswick with a minimum overall GPA of 2.0 and attend a department declaration meeting. [9]
Description: The Department of Exercise Science & Sport Studies is an undergraduate program for students working towards a Bachelor of Science degree. The program offers four options: Applied Kinesiology, Exercise Science, Exercise Physiology (three health-science, laboratory-based options), and Sports Management (a business-oriented option). The health science tracks provide a strong foundation in human anatomy and physiology, preparing students for graduate programs in medicine, physical and occupational therapy, and other health-related professions. [2] The Sports Management option provides a background in business and management, preparing students for careers in sport administration, marketing, and facilities management. [2] The overall program aims to provide a solid foundation in the sciences, develop evidence-based decision-making skills, offer real-world experience through internships, and engage students in undergraduate research. [1]
CostPerCredit: For part-time undergraduate students at the School of Arts and Sciences, the cost per credit is $482 for New Jersey residents and $1,162 for non-New Jersey residents. [12]
MinGPA: To graduate with the exercise science and sport studies major, students must have at least a 2.0 grade-point average for the applied kinesiology or sport management options, or a 3.0 for the exercise science or exercise physiology option. [36]
ScholarshipAmount: Scholarships for first-year students can range from $5,000–$16,000 per year. [2] Other available awards include the College-Sponsored Merit Scholarship at $1,000 per year and various endowed scholarships from $500–$5,000 per year. [10, 2]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Finance

[9] The curriculum covers all aspects of money management, including investment, collection, disbursement, borrowing, and fund-raising. [18] Students are trained to prepare financial reports, oversee cash flow and investments, and assess an organization's financial status. [9, 18] The program focuses on developing analytical abilities and proficiency in financial analysis methods and technology, preparing graduates for roles as financial managers who handle tasks such as directing investment activities and implementing cash management strategies. [9]
Accredidation: Rutgers Business School holds accreditation from AACSB International (The Association to Advance Collegiate Schools of Business). [2, 3]

[13]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Genetics
Requirements: First-year applicants must submit a complete application through the Rutgers Application or the Common App. [6] This includes a self-reported academic record. Description: Genetika je štúdium dedičnosti; ako sa vlastnosti živých bytostí prenášajú z jednej generácie na druhú. Ako vysokoškolák budete vykonávať výskum s renomovanými vedcami s cieľom porozumieť a prispieť k pokroku v genetike ľudí a modelových organizmov. Mnohé oblasti výskumu sa zameriavajú špecificky na identifikáciu génov, ktoré spôsobujú ochorenia u ľudí. Oblasti výučby zahŕňajú mendelovskú a komplexnú dedičnosť, molekulárnu, rakovinovú, výpočtovú, štatistickú, vývojovú, evolučnú, expresnú reguláciu, neuropsychiatrickú, neurogenetiku, populačnú, reprodukčnú, epigenetiku, genetiku a genomiku. [4] Nielenže sa naučíte pojmy, koncepty a teórie, ktoré sú základom oblasti genetiky, ale budete tiež schopní využiť to, čo ste sa naučili, na kritickú analýzu publikovaného výskumu, ako aj na vykonávanie vlastného výskumu. [4] Mnoho našich študentov je autormi prác publikovaných v popredných vedeckých časopisoch. [4]

Description: Welcome to Rutgers German! Here you will find a vibrant undergraduate and graduate program, with award-winning teaching, innovative courses, and state of the art language instruction; distinguished professors engaged in cutting-edge interdisciplinary research; an exciting slate of visiting professors and a writer-in-residence program. [7] We host two premier lecture series and encourage students to go on a top-tier study abroad program to Berlin. [7] For graduate students, we offer professional development opportunities and outstanding job placement. [7] Rutgers German is committed to creative, interdisciplinary approaches to the teaching and study of all facets of German-speaking culture from the twelfth through the twenty-first centuries. [7] In the 21st century, cultural fluency is imperative. We are training the global citizens of the future. [7]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in History
Requirements: First-year applicants must submit an application, a non-refundable application fee or fee waiver, a self-reported academic record (STARS), and a short, original essay. [2] While not required, information about extracurricular activities, employment, and community service can be included to enhance the application. [2]
Description: The major in history consists of 12 3-credit courses, for a total of 36 credits. All courses must be passed with a grade of C or better. At least six of these courses must be taken in the Rutgers–New Brunswick history department (01:506, 01:508, or 01:510 or 01:512). The major has three components: First, all majors are required to take our two-semester introductory survey, “Development of Europe” (510:201-202). Although students may take a variety of other introductory courses, and are encouraged to do so, only 510:201-202 is required for the major. Majors must also take our seminar, “Historical Studies” (506:401 or 402), in which they learn the basics of historical research and writing. Because it is a research seminar, it is normally taken in the junior or senior year. Finally, majors are required to choose a field of concentration. The concentration ensures that each of our majors has some expertise in a particular area of history. We currently offer three concentrations: 1. Global, comparative, and transnational history (the 'Global' concentration) 2. The history of the Americas, colonialism, and encounters ('Americas and Colonialism') 3. The history of gender, sexuality, and the body (the 'Gender and Body' concentration) The concentration consists of four courses. Students may choose which of their history courses they want to count for their concentration, but at least two of the four must be at the 300 level or above. No more than one of the four may be an introductory (100- or 200-level) course, and this course must be in addition to 510:201-202. The remaining four courses of the 12 required for the major are electives. Students can choose any history course they wish, including courses that are not on the list for their concentration.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Human Resource Management
Requirements: First-year applicants must submit an online application and the Self-Reported Academic Record (SRAR). An application fee is also required. Rutgers has been a test-optional institution, allowing students to choose whether to submit SAT or ACT scores.
Description: The Bachelor of Arts (B.A.) in Human Resource Management is a joint degree program offered by the School of Management and Labor Relations (SMLR) and the School of Arts and Sciences (SAS) at Rutgers University-New Brunswick. [13, 14] The curriculum is multidisciplinary, drawing from fields such as business strategy, psychology, economics, and sociology. [2] Students in the program gain exposure to a wide array of HR topics and develop marketable business skills. [2] The major requires a total of 42 credits, which includes coursework from the human resource management curriculum, related courses from other programs, and specific quantitative courses. [13] To declare the major, students must first complete the 'Introduction to Human Resource Management' course with a grade of C or better. [13, 14]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Industrial Engineering
Description: Industrial engineering involves the design and analysis of systems that include people, equipment, and materials and their interactions and performance in the workplace. An industrial engineer collects this information and evaluates alternatives to make decisions that best advance the goals of the enterprise. The program in industrial engineering offers students a base of traditional engineering courses, such as work design, human-machine systems, probability, statistics, and engineering economy, while emphasizing such contemporary areas as simulation modeling, engineering database systems, quality assurance, logistics and supply chain management, operations research, and facilities planning. Students integrate the knowledge acquired in these courses in a two-semester capstone design project.
Accredidation: The Industrial Engineering Program is accredited by the Engineering Accreditation Commission of ABET, https://www.abet.org, under the commission's General Criteria and Program Criteria for Industrial and Similarly Named Engineering Programs.

You'll develop practical computer-based competencies and unite those skills with ideas from the humanities and social sciences, equipping you to solve problems where people and machines meet. [2] Through coursework in areas like programming, social informatics, and user-centered design, you'll learn to solve complex problems and communicate solutions effectively. Description: The major in Italian is a liberal arts major designed to explore Italy’s vital role in the development of the humanistic values and disciplines that have infused Western culture over several centuries. Central to the major in Italian is the conviction that study of another language yields the important benefit of enlightening students about their own culture while instructing them about a foreign one. Core courses provide students with a solid linguistic, literary, and historical background in Italian. Additional offerings range across several disciplines, including the study of film, philosophy, comparative literature, history, political theory, art, religious studies, theater, architecture, and music.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Labor Studies and Employment Relations
Requirements: To major in Labor Studies and Employment Relations, students must first be admitted to the Rutgers School of Arts and Sciences (SAS). After admission to SAS, students can declare the major. Individuals who wish to apply for admission should contact the Office of University Undergraduate Admissions.

Concentration: ['Diversity in the Workplace', 'Labor Unions and Social Movements', 'Law and the Workplace', 'Work, Globalization, and Migration', 'Work Organization and Management']
Description: The Bachelor of Arts program in Labor Studies and Employment Relations is a broad social science major offered jointly from the School of Management and Labor Relations (SMLR) and the School of Arts and Sciences (SAS). [1] The program explores work, how it shapes society, how it is changing, and the issues it poses for employees, employers, and citizens. [2] Students learn to manage people effectively in corporate, government, or community organizations and apply knowledge of current issues like work-life balance and employee rights to the workplace. [1] The curriculum provides multiple perspectives, from managing people well to understanding how working people can address problems and how society can improve work. [2] SMLR's faculty uses real-world experience and research to engage students through small group discussions, simulations, and in-class debates. [3]
ScholarshipAmount: A variety of scholarships are available, though specific amounts for the B.A. in Labor Studies and Employment Relations are not detailed. For the online B.S. program, a Dean's Online Student Scholarship of $5,000 per year is available for eligible non-resident students. [14]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Marine Sciences
Requirements: First-year applicants must submit an application through either the Rutgers Application or the Common App. All applicants currently enrolled in high school are also required to complete a Self-Reported Academic Record (SRAR). Rutgers conducts a holistic review of each application, considering academic strength and performance, essay, and extracurricular activities.
Department: School of Environmental and Biological Sciences
Concentration: ['Marine Biology/Biological Oceanography', 'Marine Chemistry', 'Physical Oceanography', 'Marine Geology', 'Directed Marine Studies']
Description: A major in marine sciences provides students with a broad curriculum in the sciences, which demonstrates how the different disciplines can be brought to bear on understanding marine processes and managing ocean resources wisely. [3] Marine science is the study of the marine environment and its interactions with the earth, the biosphere, and the atmosphere. [1, 2] It is therefore an interdisciplinary science requiring knowledge of the principles of physics, geology and geophysics, mathematics, chemistry, and biology. [1, 2] The Major prepares students for a broad range of marine and environmental science fields, civil service careers in environmental management and consulting, or teaching in secondary schools. [1] The interdisciplinary coursework also prepares students for graduate studies in oceanography, or one of the basic science disciplines. [1] The Marine Science curriculum emphasizes improvement of oral and written communication skills and facility in accessing, reading, and understanding the current primary literature in marine sciences. [1, 2] Several courses include hands-on, experiential learning in the laboratory or in the field, and students are required to complete an experience-based education requirement. [1, 2]
Accredidation: Rutgers, The State University of New Jersey, is accredited by the Middle States Commission on Higher Education (MSCHE). [9] The university was initially accredited by MSCHE in 1921 and was most recently reaccredited in 2018. [9] There is no mention of a specific accreditation for the Bachelor of Science in Marine Sciences program itself. [9]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Marketing
Requirements: Rutgers University utilizes a holistic review process for first-year applicants, considering academic performance, a personal essay, and extracurricular activities. Submission of SAT or ACT scores is optional for most programs.
Description: Marketing is the management process through which goods and services move from concept to the a solid foundation in marketing. The Marketing major provides students the opportunity to develop skills that enable them to function in different marketing roles while working closely and effectively with other business functions. [9] With courses ranging from traditional marketing analytics and research to the new rules of digital marketing and consumer behavior, students leave the program with a solid foundation in marketing. [9, 15] Whether it is communicating offline or online, marketing is an integral part of business. [9, 15] Career opportunities in marketing are quite extensive and diversified. [9, 15] Many marketing positions give a considerable amount of discretion to people early in their careers. [9, 15]
Accredidation: The Rutgers Business School, which houses the marketing program, is accredited by the Association to Advance Collegiate Schools of Business (AACSB). [13]
CostPerCredit: $482 per credit for New Jersey residents and $1,162 per credit for non-New Jersey residents (Part-time). [40]

While specific requirements for high school coursework, GPA, and test scores can vary by the particular school and college within the university, there are some general expectations for first-year applicants. The university looks at your academic record, including your GPA and the rigor of your high school curriculum. In general, applicants should have completed at least 16 high school academic courses. Beyond academics, Rutgers considers personal essays, extracurricular activities, special talents, leadership roles, and other life experiences.
Fees: $14,933 per year for New Jersey residents and a higher rate for out-of-state students.
Description: The Bachelor of Arts in Mathematics provides a comprehensive foundation in mathematical principles and their practical applications. This degree offers courses that combine theoretical understanding with real-world problem-solving skills. Students will explore various mathematical disciplines, preparing them for diverse fields requiring analytical thinking and quantitative skills.
CostPerCredit: $482/credit hour for New Jersey residents and $1,162/credit hour for non-New Jersey residents.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Mathematics
Requirements: Rutgers conducts a holistic review of each student's application. The submission of SAT and ACT test scores is optional for most undergraduate applicants through 2026. [3, 14] If an applicant chooses not to submit a test score, they will still receive full admission consideration. [3, 14] We conduct a holistic review of each student's application that takes into consideration many more factors than test scores and cumulative grade-point averages. [14]
Fees: $14,933 per year for New Jersey residents and $35,758 for out-of-state students.
Description: Mathematics is a rigorous and demanding intellectual pursuit. It is also interesting, exciting and challenging. Majors like its clarity and the satisfaction of knowing that they have the right answer to a problem. Graduate schools in medicine, law, and business think mathematics is a great major because it develops analytical skills and the ability to work in a problem-solving environment. Their entrance tests support this bias, so the more math you know, the better you will do on their exams.
CostPerCredit: $482 per credit

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Mechanical Engineering
Requirements: For first-year applicants to the School of Engineering, the following high school coursework is required: 4 years of English, 4 years of mathematics (including algebra I, geometry, algebra II, and pre-calculus or higher), 1 year of physics, and 1 year of chemistry. A total of 16 academic courses are necessary. It is recommended that students who complete pre-calculus before their senior year take calculus. Other factors considered include the quality of the academic program, class rank, and extracurricular activities. [11] Applicants must submit their application and then complete the Self-reported Transcript and Academic Record System (STARS) Record. [10, 12]
Description: The Bachelor of Science in Mechanical Engineering program at Rutgers University has several educational objectives. Within three to five years of graduation, graduates are expected to have created value for organizations by analyzing, evaluating, and improving engineered systems using mechanical engineering methods. They should also be able to communicate effectively across different fields and contribute to managing or leading activities to meet organizational and personal goals. Graduates are also expected to solve problems using structured and unstructured mechanical engineering methodologies and to design, develop, or implement innovative systems and processes by applying engineering principles. [2] Upon finishing the program, students are expected to have the ability to identify, formulate, and solve complex engineering problems. They should also be able to apply engineering design to create solutions that meet specific needs while considering public health, safety, and welfare, as well as global, cultural, social, environmental, and economic factors. [2]
Accredidation: The Bachelor of Science and Honors Bachelor of Science in Mechanical Engineering degree programs are accredited by the Engineering Accreditation Commission of ABET, https://www.abet.org, under the commission's General Criteria and Program Criteria for Mechanical and Similarly Named Engineering Programs. [2, 3, 4]
ScholarshipType: Merit-based, Need-based, Athletic, Field-Specific, Identity-based, Community service, Military-affiliated, Employer-sponsored

Courses required for the major and minor provide a survey of the various ways scholars have approached the region, and a detailed look at the region's history, language, and culture. [7]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Music

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Philosophy
Description: Inspired by Socrates' insight that the unexamined life is not worth living, philosophy seeks answers to fundamental questions such as: What is ultimately real? What is the nature and extent of our knowledge? What is the source and nature of our moral obligations? What form of government is the best? Is beauty only in the eye of the beholder? Our undergraduate program is designed to aid students in examining these questions, and in developing and defending their own answers in the arena of reasoned controversy. [3] The major in philosophy requires courses from the core areas of history of philosophy, metaphysics, epistemology, value theory, and the philosophies of mind, language, and science. [9] Our majors advance to graduate study in many fields in addition to philosophy: law, medicine, business, education, journalism, and the sciences. [3]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Physics
Requirements: Rutgers University does not list program-specific application requirements for the Bachelor of Arts in Physics. All applicants must follow the general first-year application requirements, which include submission of the online application and a self-reported academic record (SRAR).
Description: The Bachelor of Arts in Physics, referred to as the General Option, is designed for students interested in careers in fields like high school teaching, health professions, or business/finance. [1] It provides a flexible pathway for those who wish to combine a physics background with other interests. Physics is the study of energy and the behavior of atoms and their components, examining the fundamental laws of nature. [5] Students in this program seek to understand how subatomic particles assemble and react to collisions and electromagnetic radiation. [5] The curriculum requires six intermediate physics courses, including two terms of Advanced General Physics, Intermediate Labs, and an Electronics Lab. [1]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Physics
Requirements: Rutgers conducts a holistic review of each student's application. This includes a comprehensive review of their academic performance, a required essay, and their extracurricular activities. All first-year applicants must also complete and submit a Self-Reported Academic Record (SRAR).
Description: The Bachelor of Science in Physics program is designed for students who want to pursue a career in physics or a related field. With a rigorous curriculum that includes advanced coursework in classical mechanics, electromagnetism, quantum mechanics and more, this program provides you with the knowledge and skills needed to succeed in graduate school or the workforce.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Planning and Public Policy

Description: Thank you for your interest in the Planning and Public Policy programs. Unfortunately, both the major and minor have been discontinued effective October 1, 2024. If you have any questions or concerns, please contact us at ugadmissions@ejb.rutgers.edu. The Planning and Public Policy major (762, 762D) provides students with a foundation in areas such as city dynamics, environmental aspects of cities, community health, urban poverty, public policy, housing issues, social concerns, fiscal matters, and land use planning. Students are prepared for entry-level professional management and planning positions focused on overseeing and improving public programs, such as transportation, housing, planning, the environment, finance, economic development, and urban renewal. These career paths can be found in business, government, education, banking, and nonprofit settings. This program also prepares students for graduate education in public administration, public policy, and urban planning.

Description: Political science addresses some of the fundamental problems facing human society. Questions concerning world peace, government policies aimed at achieving economic stability and growth, the management of environmental quality, control over political competition, the possibility of using law to affect social and political change, and the gap between the rich and poor in the U.S. and abroad are all on the research agenda of contemporary political scientists. [1]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Portuguese
Requirements: For admission to the School of Arts and Sciences, where the Portuguese major is housed, applicants must complete a high school curriculum with at least 16 academic units. [2, 15] Rutgers conducts a holistic review of each student's application. [15]
Description: The program summary states that Portuguese is the official language of 10 countries on four continents. [12] The major provides the opportunity to develop Portuguese language skills while studying the literature and culture of Portugal, Brazil, and African lands of Portuguese language or influence. [12] Undergraduate courses offer the chance to develop proficiency in speaking, comprehension, reading, and writing in Portuguese. [15]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Psychology
Description: The curriculum for the B.A. in Psychology is designed for students with an interest in human behavior, social and community services, personality theories, developmental issues, and a wide variety of other focus areas. Students have room to tailor their degree to match their postgraduate plans. For example, the B.A. curriculum combined with additional courses in research methods, hands-on research experience, and writing intensive courses provides solid preparation for graduate studies in psychology. [14]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Public Health
Requirements: Prospective first-year students apply to Rutgers University through the general admissions process. The Bachelor of Science in Public Health is offered through the Edward J. Bloustein School of Planning and Public Policy. While there are no specific application requirements listed for first-year students for this major, general application materials for Rutgers typically include a high school transcript, an application essay, and letters of recommendation. Admission to the major for transfer students and those changing schools within Rutgers requires a minimum of 30 credits and a cumulative GPA of at least 2.5.
Department: Edward J. Bloustein School of Planning and Public Policy
Fees: {'In-State': '$14,933 per year', 'Out-of-State': None}
Description: The Bachelor of Science in Public Health requires a minimum of 120 credits. To meet these requirements, public health majors must satisfy the college group requirements, the university general education requirements and the overall public health program requirements. The nature of the public health curriculum gives students the freedom to focus on health-related topics that interest them, propelling their path toward a suitable career in the health professions. The public health degree program incorporates core courses in topics such as biostatistics, epidemiology, environmental health and behavioral aspects of public health. Each of these intersecting subjects works to teach students how to improve the quality of life in their community and beyond. Through the public health degree program, you learn how to assess and prevent health disparities. You'll also find yourself exploring various health-related topics with courses centered around the well-being of individuals, communities, populations and the world. The Bachelor of Science in Public Health practicum provides an opportunity for students to synthesize, integrate and apply practical skills, knowledge and training learned through courses, gain professional experience in a public health work environment and work on public health practice projects that are of particular interest to them.
CostPerCredit: $482/credit

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Puerto Rican and Hispanic Caribbean Studies
Requirements: General requirements for first-year applicants include submitting an application, a non-refundable $70 application fee, a self-reported academic record, and an original essay. [7] High school records must show at least 16 academic units: 4 years of English, 3 years of mathematics (including Algebra I, Geometry, and Algebra II), 2 years of science, 2 years of a single foreign language, and 5 other academic courses. [8]
Fees: For the 2025–2026 academic year, tuition for New Jersey residents at the Rutgers University–New Brunswick School of Arts and Sciences is $14,933. [12] Fees are an additional $3,891. [12]
Description: The Department of Puerto Rican and Hispanic Caribbean Studies offers an interdisciplinary program of studies that examines the diverse political, social, and cultural histories of the Spanish-speaking societies of the Caribbean as well as Latino communities in the United States. [2] Using a comparative approach, the curriculum focuses on the formation and evolution of the peoples and societies of the region. [2] Courses examine the gender, racial, class, and cultural dimensions of the migration experience of Caribbean peoples and the reformulation of national identities. [2] The curriculum fosters critical thinking about how knowledge is created, different methods and modes of analysis, and the limitations of traditional disciplinary approaches. It does so while developing competencies in research, analysis, and written as well as oral presentations. [2]
CostPerCredit: For part-time students in the School of Arts and Sciences, the cost per credit hour is $482 for New Jersey residents and $1,162 for non-New Jersey residents. [12]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Religion
Requirements: General requirements for first-year applicants include the submission of an application, a non-refundable application fee, a self-reported academic record (STARS), and an original essay. [2, 6] The high school record must show at least 16 academic units, including 4 years of English, 3 years of mathematics, 2 years of science, and 2 years of a foreign language. [5]
Description: The study of religion is very interdisciplinary. Drawing on insights from anthropology, art, history, literature, philosophy, science, and sociology, among others, the department helps students develop a comprehensive and nuanced understanding of religion—how it works in people's lives and its impact on societies in the past and in the present. [18] As a religion graduate you are expected to have an appreciation of the diversity of humanity's religious traditions. [12] You will also be able to identify and coherently discuss the conceptual issues that shape the academic study of religion. [12] The field of religious studies is closely related to anthropology, sociology, theology, psychology, philosophy, literature, cultural studies, art history, history, and area studies such as South Asian Studies, Africana Studies, and Middle Eastern Studies. [19] The Religion Department at Rutgers University provides a rich setting for the secular academic study of religion. [19]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Russian
Requirements: Specific application requirements such as a resume or statement of purpose for the Bachelor of Arts in Russian are not specified on the Rutgers University website. Applicants are expected to complete the general first-year application.

Description: The major in Russian Language and Literature aims to provide a solid foundation in the Russian language and a broad, interdisciplinary introduction to the culture of Russian-speaking regions. [16] The program's particular strength is Russophone literary culture during the Imperial, Soviet, and post-Soviet periods, grounding the study of literature and film in specific historical, social, and cultural contexts. [20] It includes the study of elements of literary and cultural theory and fosters a broad interdisciplinary perspective by encouraging students to take relevant courses in fields such as history, philosophy, political science, art history, and music. [16] Russian majors are expected to achieve a degree of language fluency that will enable them to enter into dialogue with regions where Russian is used, as readers, writers, and speakers of a language native to over 170 million people around the world. [13] Coursework includes materials in the original ranging from literary classics to current journalism and other mass media. [13] The program offers a major and three minor tracks in Russian language and literature, and an interdisciplinary minor in Slavic and East European Studies. [11] We also teach a wide range of literature and culture courses entirely in English. [11]
CostPerCredit: $482 per credit for New Jersey residents and $1,162 per credit for non-New Jersey residents for part-time enrollment in the School of Arts and Sciences. [15]
ScholarshipAmount: Rutgers offers endowed scholarships ranging from $500–$5,000 per year.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Social Work
Requirements: Students are admitted to the major at the beginning of their junior year, after having completed approximately 60 credits of coursework. Students should plan to apply to the major early in the spring semester of their sophomore year. A cumulative grade-point average of 3.0 is required for acceptance into the program. [9]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Sociology
Requirements: For admission to undergraduate schools at Rutgers, the high school record must show at least 16 academic units, including 4 years of English, 2 years of a foreign language, 3 years of mathematics (including Algebra I, Geometry, Algebra II), 2 years of science, and 5 other academic courses. [10] First-year students who are currently enrolled in high school are also required to submit a Self-reported Transcript and Academic Record System (STARS) Record. [2, 6] The application can be submitted through the Rutgers Application or the Common App. [6]
Description: Sociology is the scientific study of social life. Sociologists seek to understand the structure of societies and the processes of social interaction that occur within them. They examine the social causes and consequences of human behavior, as groups and as individuals. The field of sociology covers a very broad range of topics, from the intimate family to the giant, global economy; from the experience of illness to the social construction of health; from the social dynamics of a city street to the social forces that are remaking the urban and rural worlds; from the divisions of race, gender, and social class to the shared beliefs of a common culture. For students, sociology provides an opportunity to develop a unique perspective on the world—the sociological imagination—that provides a powerful tool for making sense of their own lives and the complex world in which they live.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Spanish
Description: The Spanish Program provides students with a world-class competence in the language, literatures and cultures of the Spanish-speaking world, which gives students a special preparedness for life in an increasingly globalized world. The Spanish Program at Rutgers-Camden offers both a Major (36 credits) and a Minor (18 credits) in Spanish. [25] We offer a complete language program with course offerings that include elementary, intermediate and advanced levels and a comprehensive list of classes in Spanish and Latin American literature, linguistics, culture and film. [25] Rutgers University has long been recognized as a leading national center for the study of languages, literature and culture. [22] Our program encompasses elementary, intermediate and advanced language courses. [22] Its purpose is to develop student skills in communication across ethnic, ideological and national boundaries, as well as, help students acquire a deeper understanding of other cultures. [22] Our program also addresses the professional needs of Camden scholars with our Spanish for Health Professionals courses, providing students with the linguistic and cultural tools needed to succeed in a Spanish-speaking environment. [25]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Statistics
Requirements: Rutgers University requires first-year applicants to submit a self-reported academic record, a high school transcript, and an application essay. While not explicitly required for all applicants, some programs may require additional essays or information. Applicants are encouraged to check the specific requirements for their intended school or college within the university.
Fees: $14,933/Year for New Jersey Residents for the 2025-2026 academic year. [11]
Description: Statistics is the science of learning from data. Statisticians are in high demand in a wide variety of fields, including business, finance, insurance, medicine, public health, government, and high-tech industry. The B.A. in statistics provides a path to a career as a statistician, and it is a great choice of a second major that will help you to stand out from the crowd in your primary field. B.A. students have a great deal of flexibility in designing their course of study. They can choose an applied or theoretical focus, pursue a minor, and/or combine their study of statistics with a major in another discipline. The B.A. can be completed in as few as eight courses totaling 27 credits.
CostPerCredit: $482/credit hour for the School of Arts and Sciences (In-state). [11]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Statistics
Requirements: Rutgers University does not list specific prerequisite courses for admission to the Bachelor of Science in Statistics program. General admission is based on a holistic review of an applicant's high school record, including the rigor of the curriculum, academic performance, and standardized test scores (if submitted).
Description: The Rutgers University undergraduate program in statistics provides students with a foundational understanding of the concepts and methods of statistical analysis. The curriculum is designed to prepare students for careers in business, industry, or government, as well as for graduate studies in statistics or related fields. Students engage with topics such as problem-solving, multivariate analysis, and probability. The program of study includes courses in survey sampling, experimental design, quality control, and biostatistics, combined with courses in mathematical statistics and probability theory. The department encourages interdisciplinary study and offers both a statistics major and a joint statistics/mathematics major.
CostPerCredit: $482/credit hour for the School of Arts and Sciences.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Fine Arts in Theater Arts
Requirements: First-year applicants must either complete and submit the Rutgers University Application or apply to Rutgers University on the Common Application. All applicants to the acting program will be required to submit a Talent Assessment which includes a $45 audition fee, an acting questionnaire, a resume, a photograph, and an audition.

Description: The bachelor of fine arts (B.F.A.) degree in theater arts is designed for students seeking intensive conservatory theater training in a setting where they have access to rigorous liberal arts courses and the cultural life and contacts of a major university. [3] The program offers three areas of study: acting, design, and production and management. [3] Students in the B.F.A. program specializing in design or production and management must be in residence for a minimum of three years. In acting, a four-year residency is required. [3] Theater is a multidimensional art form requiring creativity, collaboration, and craft. [10] The commitment in the Theater Department at Mason Gross School of the Arts is to educate, guide and foster the aspiring theater professional and provide uniquely individualized instruction and practical experience, including intensive studio classes, innovative academic curricula, and productions. [10]
ScholarshipAmount: Mason Gross undergraduate scholarship typically ranges between $2,000 and $10,000 per year. [4]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Urban Studies
Requirements: For admission to the Edward J. Bloustein School of Planning and Public Policy to pursue a major in urban studies, students must apply after completing 40 credits. [2] Successful applicants typically have an overall grade-point average of 2.5 or better and an average grade of at least 2.5 in the prerequisite courses. [2] First-year applicants to Rutgers must complete the application and the Self-reported Transcript and Academic Record System (STARS). [6] General high school course requirements for entrance to most undergraduate schools at Rutgers include 4 years of English, 3 years of mathematics, 2 years of science, and 2 years of a foreign language, totaling at least 16 academic units. [5]
Department: Edward J. Bloustein School of Planning and Public Policy
Description: The Bloustein School offers major and minor programs in urban studies, leading to a bachelor of arts degree. Urban studies prepares students for graduate education in urban planning and policy development and for entry-level positions in the public and private sectors, especially jobs in housing, transportation, and community development. To pursue a major in urban studies, students must apply and be admitted to the Edward J. Bloustein School of Planning and Public Policy.
